name: RA-DIT (Retrieval-Augmented Dual Instruction Tuning)
venue: ICLR 2024 (The Twelfth International Conference on Learning Representations, Vienna, Austria, May 7-11, 2024; OpenReview id 22OTbutug9). Preprint arXiv:2310.01352 (v1 2 Oct 2023; v4 ICLR 2024 camera-ready, 6 May 2024). DBLP: conf/iclr/Lin0CSL00KSLZY24.
authors_affiliation: Xi Victoria Lin, Xilun Chen, Mingda Chen (equal contribution), Weijia Shi, Maria Lomeli, Rich(ard) James, Pedro Rodriguez, Jacob Kahn, Gergely Szilvasy, Mike Lewis, Luke Zettlemoyer, Wen-tau (Scott) Yih. Affiliation: FAIR at Meta (Weijia Shi is also affiliated with the University of Washington). Corresponding/lead emails: {victorialin,xilun,mingdachen,scottyih}@meta.com.
code_url: https://github.com/facebookresearch/RA-DIT (official data-preparation artifact release, ICLR 2024; CC-BY-NC license; Python 99.5%; releases fine-tuning dataset processing scripts and the DRAGON+ embeddings of the Wiki-2021 index, plus prompt-generation code. It is a partial/WIP artifact: retriever setup and training are marked WIP and full LM/retriever training code is not included.)
maintained_repo_url: N/A (single-paper official artifact repo; not a continuously-updated leaderboard or paper list).
task_domain: QA / knowledge-intensive NLP. Retrieval-augmented language modeling (RALM) for knowledge-intensive zero- and few-shot tasks: open-domain QA (Natural Questions, TriviaQA), multiple-choice knowledge (MMLU), multi-hop QA (HotpotQA), fact verification (FEVER), entity linking (AIDA CoNLL-YAGO), slot filling (Zero-Shot RE, T-REx), long-form QA (ELI5), and knowledge-grounded dialogue (Wizard of Wikipedia). Not an agentic/planning/tool-use/embodied setting.
problem_setting: Offline, single-model (single-agent), non-interactive setting. The goal is to retrofit any pre-trained auto-regressive LLM (Llama 7B/13B/65B) with retrieval capability via a lightweight two-step fine-tuning recipe, as a cheaper alternative to expensive end-to-end RALM pre-training (REALM, RETRO, Atlas) and to suboptimal post-hoc/off-the-shelf fusion (REPLUG, In-Context RALM). Supervision is available: multi-task instruction-tuning data (20 datasets across dialogue, open-domain QA, reading comprehension, summarization, chain-of-thought) plus unsupervised corpus text. Two decoupled fine-tuning steps: (1) LM-ft (RA-IT) updates the LLM to better use retrieved 'background' context and to ignore distractors; (2) R-ft updates the retriever's query encoder via LM-Supervised Retrieval (LSR) so retrieved chunks better match LLM preferences. Evaluation is primarily zero-/few-shot on held-out knowledge-intensive benchmarks not seen during fine-tuning. The retrieval corpus is a fixed external store (Wikipedia + CommonCrawl); there is no test-time interaction or growing agent memory.
what_is_retrieved: Documents / text chunks (passages, max 200 words each) from an external corpus that provide factual 'background' knowledge to ground the LLM's prediction. Not demonstrations, tools, cases, trajectories, skills, or agent experiences.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a fixed retrieval data store of 399M text chunks combining the Dec 20, 2021 Wikipedia dump (from Izacard et al. 2022, Atlas) with the 2017-2020 CommonCrawl dumps. There is no growing/episodic agent memory; the store is read-only and not written to by the system during deployment.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k document ranking. The retriever returns top-k relevant text chunks (k tuned: top-1/3/10 studied, with performance improving as k grows; k-tilde=3 used to build LM-ft data). The objective is similarity/effectiveness-style top-k retrieval whose chunks are then ensembled (weighted by relevance score), not recovery of a minimal complete set nor a precision-driven variable-size set. The R-ft (LSR) objective trains the retriever to rank chunks by how much they improve the LLM's likelihood of the correct answer.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve] only. RA-DIT retrieves documents to ground generation; there is no case Reuse/Revise/Retain in the CBR sense (no case library, no case adaptation, no retention of solved cases). Not a CBR method.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False: RA-DIT does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It is a retrieval-augmented LM fine-tuning method.
retrieval_unit: Document / text chunk (a passage of up to 200 words) retrieved by dense similarity. Each retrieved chunk is the unit prepended as a 'Background:' field to the LLM prompt.
index_source: Static external corpus, offline-induced. A 399M-chunk dense index built from Wikipedia 2021 (Atlas snapshot) + 2017-2020 CommonCrawl, encoded with the DRAGON+ document encoder; ANN search via FAISS / Atlas distributed index (the released embeddings use an IVF65536/PQ256 index). No online/test-time growth driven by the model.
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index (single-vector dual-encoder embeddings, dot-product / nearest-neighbor search; FAISS IVF-PQ in the released index). No graph, hierarchy, or cluster topology.
retriever_type: Dense dual-encoder retriever (single-vector bi-encoder). Initialized with DRAGON+ (Lin et al. 2023), a state-of-the-art dense retriever trained with contrastive learning and data augmentation. Then made LEARNED via R-ft: the query encoder is fine-tuned with LM supervision (LSR). So overall: dense + learned (LM-feedback-trained query encoder).
retriever_learning_signal: Two-fold. Initialization: contrastive similarity training (off-the-shelf DRAGON+). Then RA-DIT's R-ft uses LM-feedback / downstream-effectiveness supervision: a generalized LM-Supervised Retrieval (LSR, from REPLUG) objective. For each (x,y), the LSR target distribution p_LSR(c|x,y) is the softmax over LM likelihoods p_LM(y | c o x)/tau of the correct answer given each candidate chunk; the retriever score distribution p_R(c|x) is trained to minimize KL(p_R || p_LSR). A higher LSR score means a chunk more improves the LLM's chance of predicting the correct answer, so the retriever is aligned to LLM preferences. Generalized beyond REPLUG by mixing unsupervised corpus data with multi-task instruction (MTI) data; best mixture is 95% corpus + 5% MTI. Only the query encoder is updated (fine-tuning both encoders hurt performance). Not RL/value-based.
query_construction: The retrieval query/key is the language model prompt x, formed from task inputs via manually constructed templates (e.g., the standalone question for QA). At LM-ft and inference time, the top-k chunks retrieved on x are prepended to x. The paper notes automatically generating task-specific retrieval queries is left to future work; queries are template-built from the raw task input, not decomposed or expanded.
query_granularity: Task-level (one-shot at t=0): a single retrieval is performed on the full task prompt; there is no per-step / per-sentence / iterative query reconstruction. (A preliminary iterative dual-tuning variant was tried but yielded no gains.)
when_to_retrieve: One-shot: retrieval is performed once on the input prompt (top-k chunks), both during LM-ft data construction and at inference. No iterative, active (uncertainty-triggered), or learned-router retrieval scheduling.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule / always-on: retrieval is always invoked once per prompt (no confidence/uncertainty trigger, no learned classifier, no reflection tokens, no agent-initiated request). The only learned 'when/what' signal is offline in R-ft, where LM likelihood (LSR score) supervises which chunks the retriever should prefer; but the decision to retrieve is unconditional at runtime.
reranking: No explicit separate reranking stage. Retrieved top-k chunks are kept; their retriever similarity scores are re-normalized (softmax over the top-k) and used as ensemble mixture weights p_R(c|x). R-ft implicitly improves ranking by aligning retriever scores to LM-preference (LSR), but there is no cross-encoder/hierarchy-aware reranker.
retrieved_context_refinement: Minimal / none in the classic sense. Each retrieved chunk is prepended verbatim as a 'Background:' field (demarcated by 'Background:' ... '\n\n'). No decomposition, distillation, compression, or distractor filtering of returned text. Robustness to distracting chunks is instead handled at the LLM side via retrieval-augmented instruction tuning (training the LM to ignore irrelevant chunks and fall back on parametric knowledge), and via parallel ensembling rather than concatenation. The SQuAD-2.0 'I don't know' training also helps the model abstain on wrong passages.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools/skills; retrieved items are raw Wikipedia/CommonCrawl text chunks, not engineered tool descriptions).
index_content_separation: N/A / No: the dense vector index maps directly to passage text; there is no lightweight-index-then-content progressive-disclosure separation (chunks are retrieved and prepended directly).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index/protocol). The retrieval corpus is a static, offline-built dense index (Wikipedia 2021 + CommonCrawl, 399M chunks); no MCP / RapidAPI / RESTful / function-calling tool integration or live sync.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools; no inter-tool dependency modeling).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation PLUS training signal (dual). (a) Utilization: each of the top-k retrieved chunks is prepended to the prompt as a 'Background:' field; the LLM computes predictions for each augmented prompt in PARALLEL and the final output probability is a relevance-weighted mixture: p_LM(y|x,C') = sum_{c in C'} p_LM(y | c o x) * p_R(c|x) (parallel in-context retrieval-augmentation, following REPLUG). (b) Training: retrieval augmentation is baked into LM fine-tuning (RA-IT, minimize -sum_i sum_j log p_LM(y_i | c_ij o x_i)), and LM likelihood feeds back as the LSR training signal for the retriever. No latent-token injection or cross-attention; pure in-context conditioning + fine-tuning.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-generate (one-shot), no planning/search loop. There is no explicit planner, MCTS, tree search, or per-step interleaving. For a prompt: retrieve top-k once, build k parallel augmented prompts, ensemble the LM outputs. Both LM-ft and R-ft are offline training stages; inference is a single retrieve-then-predict pass.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer: a single retrieval per input prompt grounds the full answer; retrieval is not interleaved per CoT-step, per-sentence, per-token, or per-tool-call. (CoT-reasoning datasets appear in the LM-ft training mix, but retrieval at inference is still one-shot per prompt.)
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR method; no case adaptation). The nearest analog is parallel ensembling of multiple retrieved chunks weighted by relevance, plus LM fine-tuning to integrate/ignore retrieved content.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw retrieved document/passage text, injected as a natural-language 'Background:' field prepended to the instruction prompt. No distilled strategy, workflow, executable program, structured note, or latent/soft-token representation.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw document/passage (un-distilled factual text chunk from Wikipedia/CommonCrawl). Not a distilled strategy/insight, state-aware guideline, reusable workflow, procedural skill, demonstration, or hint.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Retriever-aware LM training plus abstention. (1) Retrieval-augmented instruction tuning (RA-IT) deliberately trains the LLM on (correct chunk, sometimes incorrect chunk) -> correct answer, so the model learns to exploit relevant context and to ignore distracting/misleading chunks by leaning on parametric knowledge (cites Shi et al. 2023a 'large language models can be easily distracted'). (2) The SQuAD-2.0 reading-comprehension data trains the model to answer 'I don't know' when the passage is irrelevant, inducing abstention when the retriever errs. (3) Preserving parametric knowledge (commonsense-reasoning eval shows no degradation) is framed as a safety net for retriever mistakes. (4) Parallel ensembling weighted by relevance reduces reliance on any single noisy chunk. No separate relevance-evaluator/self-reflection module or reason-in-documents distillation.
memory_type: none (no episodic/skill/workflow/procedural/graph/latent agent memory). The external 399M-chunk corpus is a static knowledge source, not an agent-written memory.
write_back: False: RA-DIT does not store new experiences, cases, or skills into any memory at deployment; it only reads from a fixed external corpus. (The retriever's query encoder is updated offline during R-ft training, but that is parameter learning, not memory write-back.)
online_growth: No: the retrievable store (399M Wikipedia + CommonCrawl chunks) is fixed/offline-built and does not grow during deployment/test-time.
write_back_trigger: never (no write-back; no episodic memory is maintained or updated at runtime).
failure_experience_usage: Partial, training-time only and not stored as memory. RA-IT exposes the LLM to imperfect/incorrect retrieved chunks during fine-tuning (and trains 'I don't know' abstention via SQuAD 2.0) so it is robust to failed retrievals, and the LSR signal down-weights chunks that lower answer likelihood. But there is no stored/retrieved repository of failed experiences; this is a static training behavior, not success+failure memory contrast at inference.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no stored runtime memory entries to mutate; append-only-none). Model/retriever parameters are updated only during offline fine-tuning, not as evolving memory.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partially: the retriever (query encoder) is LEARNED via LM-supervised LSR (KL to the LM-preference distribution), so 'what to retrieve' is trained from LM feedback rather than fixed similarity. However, it is an offline-trained dense scoring function, not an RL/value-based or M-MDP soft-Q retrieval policy, and the decision of WHEN to retrieve remains a fixed top-k schedule.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No: single-model, single private retriever+LM pipeline; no memory/experience shared across agents or heterogeneous frameworks.
benchmarks: Knowledge-intensive (held out from fine-tuning): MMLU; Natural Questions (NQ); TriviaQA (TQA); ELI5; and a 7-task KILT subset: HotpotQA (HoPo), FEVER (FEV), AIDA CoNLL-YAGO (AIDA), Zero-Shot RE (zsRE), T-REx, Wizard of Wikipedia (WoW) (and ELI5). Commonsense reasoning (no retrieval): BoolQ, PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, OpenBookQA (OBQA). Comparison setting also uses Atlas's 64-shot KILT-style fine-tuning on 8 tasks (NQ, TQA, HoPo, FEV, AIDA, zsRE, T-REx, WoW).
benchmark_family: QA / multi-hop / knowledge-intensive NLP. Spans MMLU (multiple-choice knowledge), open-domain QA (NQ, TQA), multi-hop QA (HotpotQA), fact verification (FEVER), entity linking (AIDA), slot filling (zsRE, T-REx), long-form QA (ELI5), knowledge-grounded dialogue (WoW) -- i.e., the KILT family -- plus a standard commonsense-reasoning suite. Not in the web/embodied/tool/code/memory-agent/decision-RL benchmark families.
baselines: Primary: base Llama (7B/13B/65B) and Llama+REPLUG (Llama 65B + off-the-shelf DRAGON+, parallel in-context RA but no fine-tuning), in 0-shot and 5-shot in-context settings. Cross-architecture: Atlas 11B (encoder-decoder RALM jointly pre-trained with its retriever) in a 64-shot fine-tuning setting. Internal ablation baselines: IT (conventional instruction tuning, no retrieval), RA-IT (retrieval-augmented IT), LM-ft-only, R-ft-only; retriever ablations vs Contriever and Contriever-MSMARCO; also referenced/compared qualitatively to InstructRetro 48B and SAIL.
key_metrics: Exact Match / accuracy for QA and classification tasks (NQ, TQA, HoPo, FEV, AIDA, zsRE, T-REx EM-style; MMLU accuracy), task-appropriate KILT metrics for WoW and ELI5 (e.g., F1/ROUGE-style scoring per KILT), and averages: Avg-diamond (MMLU, NQ, TQA, ELI5) and overall Avg across the 10 knowledge-intensive tasks. Commonsense tasks use accuracy. Improvements reported as average percentage-point gains.
headline_result: RA-DIT 65B sets state-of-the-art on knowledge-intensive zero-/few-shot benchmarks, outperforming the un-tuned in-context RALM REPLUG (Llama 65B + DRAGON+) by +8.9% on average 0-shot and +1.4% 5-shot (averaged over MMLU, NQ, TQA, ELI5). Per-task 0-shot vs REPLUG: MMLU +8.2% (64.6 vs 59.7), NQ +22% (relative; 35.2 vs 28.8), e.g. zsRE 73.7 vs 50.8, T-REx 53.1 vs 36.3. In the 64-shot fine-tuned setting, a single RA-DIT 65B model beats task-specific Atlas 11B by +4.1 points on average (60.9 vs 56.8) over 8 KILT tasks, winning on 6/8.
ablations: 1) Dual instruction tuning ablation (Table 6, 5-shot dev): both LM-ft (RIT 65B + Dragon+, Avg 53.9) and R-ft (Llama 65B + FTed Dragon+, Avg 54.4) alone beat the REPLUG baseline (Llama 65B + Dragon+, Avg 53.8); combining both (RA-DIT, RIT 65B + FTed Dragon+, Avg 54.6) is best (+0.8 over baseline). 2) LM fine-tuning strategy (Table 4): RA-IT > IT > base Llama with retrieval; at 0-shot top-10 chunks RA-IT 65B 51.0 vs IT 65B 47.7; instruction tuning alone helps 0-shot but is marginal/hurts 5-shot; performance rises monotonically with more retrieved chunks (top-1<top-3<top-10). 3) Retriever fine-tuning data (Table 5): corpus data alone +0.4, MTI data alone +0.1; best is 95% corpus + 5% MTI (Avg 58.0 vs 57.4 base Dragon+); fine-tuning BOTH encoders hurts (54.0) vs query-encoder only -> only the query encoder is updated. 4) Retriever choice (Table 7): Dragon+ (Avg 53.4) > Contriever-MSMARCO (51.8) > Contriever (47.5) > Llama no-retrieval (45.0). 5) Commonsense reasoning (Table 3): RA-DIT 65B improves over Llama 65B on 7/8 tasks (Avg 74.5 vs 72.1), showing parametric knowledge is preserved. 6) Appendix: RA-IT gives even larger boosts on smaller Llama 7B/13B (scaling-laws analysis); retrieval-corpora ablation shows Wiki-2021-only retains most of the benefit vs full Wiki+CC. Iterative/multi-step RA-DIT was tried but gave no further gains.
evaluation_decoupling: No: only end-to-end downstream task metrics (EM/accuracy/KILT scores and their averages) are reported. No separate intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG) for the retriever are reported; retriever quality is assessed indirectly through downstream task gains (e.g., the retriever-choice and R-ft ablations).
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Outcome only: final-answer task metrics. There is no scored intermediate process metric (no reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise retrieval-accuracy scoring). The number of retrieved chunks (top-1/3/10) ablation and qualitative appendix examples (model ignoring wrong chunks / answering 'I don't know') touch on process behavior but are not quantified as process metrics.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Framed as a 'lightweight' alternative: RA-DIT avoids the expensive end-to-end RALM pre-training of REALM/RETRO/Atlas, needing only two short fine-tuning steps over downstream data. A single multi-task RA-DIT 65B model beats task-specific Atlas 11B (which needs joint pre-training + per-task fine-tuning). Inference uses parallel in-context augmentation over k chunks (k=1/3/10), adding moderate cost that scales with k; accuracy rises with more chunks. The released artifact notes the Wiki-2021-only index retains most performance vs the full 399M Wiki+CC index, reducing storage. No explicit GPU-hour, dollar, or latency numbers are reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed top-k, capped by context window. Each retrieved chunk is <=200 words and prepended as a 'Background:' field; predictions over k augmented prompts are computed in parallel (not concatenated), so each prompt holds one chunk plus the instruction, sidestepping a single long-context budget. LM-ft data is built with k-tilde=3 retrieved chunks per example (k-tilde+1 for self-contained RC tasks that also have a gold passage). Inference k is fixed and ablated (top-1/3/10), with k=10 strongest at 0-shot.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing benchmarks; constructs no new dataset). Notable resource scale: fine-tuning over 20 datasets (LM-ft set D_L) and a QA-focused retriever-ft set D_R (adds FreebaseQA, MS MARCO Q-A pairs); retrieval corpus = 399M text chunks (Wikipedia 2021 + 2017-2020 CommonCrawl), max 200 words each.
builds_on: REPLUG (Shi et al. 2023b) -- parallel in-context retrieval-augmentation, relevance-weighted output mixture, and the LM-Supervised Retrieval (LSR) objective that RA-DIT generalizes; In-Context RALM (Ram et al. 2023); DRAGON+ dense retriever (Lin et al. 2023) as retriever init; Llama (Touvron et al. 2023a) as the LM backbone; instruction-tuning / label-loss objective (Chung et al. 2022b; Iyer et al. 2022 OPT-IML); 'LMs easily distracted by irrelevant context' (Shi et al. 2023a) motivating distractor-robust LM-ft; FAISS / Atlas index (Izacard et al. 2022) and the Atlas Wikipedia corpus. Conceptually positioned among RALMs: REALM (Guu et al. 2020), RETRO (Borgeaud et al. 2022), Atlas (Izacard et al. 2022b), RAG (Lewis et al. 2020), FiD (Izacard & Grave 2021).
contrasts_with: REPLUG / In-Context RALM (off-the-shelf fusion of frozen LLM + general retriever) -- RA-DIT argues this is suboptimal because the LLM is not trained to use retrieved content; RA-DIT fine-tunes both. Atlas / REALM / RETRO (expensive end-to-end or continuous RALM pre-training) -- RA-DIT is lightweight fine-tuning that competes without pre-training. SAIL (Luo et al. 2023, most related) -- fine-tunes a 7B LM on retrieval-augmented instructions but concatenates passages in-context and uses non-differentiable BM25; RA-DIT instead uses parallel multi-passage augmentation, a learnable neural retriever, and dual optimization. Self-RAG (Asai et al. 2023) -- adaptive on-demand retrieval with reflection tokens, vs RA-DIT's fixed one-shot retrieval. InstructRetro / RETRO+IT (Wang et al. 2023) -- fine-tunes a cross-attention RETRO LM while freezing memory encoder, vs RA-DIT decoupling and tuning both LM and retriever in the in-context framework.
lineage: Group B (RAG for task solving). A lineage member of in-context retrieval-augmented LMs that adds lightweight fine-tuning: it extends REPLUG's parallel in-context augmentation and LSR by jointly (but decoupled) tuning the LLM (to use retrieved context and ignore distractors) and the retriever (to LLM preferences). Sits between off-the-shelf RALM fusion (REPLUG, In-Context RALM) and heavyweight pre-trained RALMs (Atlas, RETRO), and alongside concurrent retrieval-aware instruction-tuning / adaptive-RAG work (SAIL, Self-RAG, InstructRetro). Establishes 'dual instruction tuning' as a practical retrofitting recipe.
